title: C504 — Master window control switch connector
introduction:
The master window switch is a busy little reception desk for the door: this reference includes window commands, mirror controls and communication with the door module. I use the connector drawing to locate a cavity label, then read the matching assignment row to understand the circuit's named job. The LIN bus is a local communication link carrying messages, so that entry should not be read as an ordinary switched power feed.

Start with the identification table, then the connector face and its harness identification, and finally the assignment table. Keep the cavity label and circuit identifier together; a wire color alone is not a circuit's identity. Repeated cavity labels and repeated function descriptions remain exactly as printed, without assuming that they describe connections fitted together on every vehicle.

This is a guide to reading the reference. Physical viewing direction, access, electrical test conditions and repair methods require the applicable service information. Gauge conventions and the meanings of Size and Used are not defined here; I retain their printed notation without using them to choose wire, probes or replacement parts.

The summary lists Pin Count 21, while the drawing labels cavities 1–20. The supplied reference does not reconcile those counts; I do not treat the summary as proof of an extra physical position.

edits.why: I use the tall housing outline and the large loop-shaped projection on the drawing's left to recognize the drawing's arrangement before following the cavity labels. These are visible housing features, with no release or locking function assigned here. The labels descend in parallel columns. Gray-filled positions correspond to assignment rows with blank circuit and function fields, providing a useful cross-check between picture and table. The drawing's page orientation does not establish which physical side of a disconnected connector faces the viewer.

Cavity links each row to the drawing; Circuit Number identifies the associated circuit; Function describes its named role. Read Color, Gauge, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number across that same row rather than combining neighboring entries. The functions distinguish window commands, mirror movement and common motor connections, door-module communication, ground, driver-switch return and a fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply. Preserve the mirror entries' IF PLUS condition; it is not permission to assume a particular polarity during a test. A blank Qualifier does not resolve which repeated assignment applies. The repeated rear-window descriptions also remain as printed, without relabeling either pair as the opposite side. Once the relevant row is understood, any testing or repair needs the matching vehicle configuration and service procedure.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count differs from the number of distinct cavity labels shown in the connector face. The assignment table repeats a cavity label, but the evidence does not explain whether Pin Count represents assignment rows or physical positions. Clarify the count's meaning before describing it as the housing's physical pin total.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all42 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and2 edits. PinCount21 versus pictured1–20 and duplicated cavity11 uncertainty retained for bounded identification reading only.
